definition: A progressive-ratio schedule is a way of rewarding an instrumental action, such as lever pressing for food, that is used to examine how strongly an animal will keep responding for the reward. In this packet, performance under this schedule is treated as an index of motivation for the appetitive behavior.

reasons: The supplied packet supports an animal-behavior reinforcement schedule, not a diagnosis-related sense; the field "diagnosis" is not defensible here.

The definition adds a general explanation of what the schedule is used to measure, but the packet only supports its use in this specific rat study as an index of motivation for appetitive instrumental behavior.

The packet does not support describing the term as part of a “diagnosis” field; it reports effects in adult rats on appetitive instrumental behavior under a progressive ratio schedule, without any diagnostic framework.

The definition’s general claim that progressive-ratio schedules are “a way of rewarding an instrumental action… that is used to examine how strongly an animal will keep responding” is not explicitly stated in the packet; the packet only mentions lever pressing “rewarded by a food outcome under a progressive ratio schedule” and refers to “acquisition or motivation,” not the broader methodological purpose as a definition.

The definition’s final clause (“treated as an index of motivation”) is only partially supported: the packet states that repeated administration “did not affect the acquisition or motivation” under the schedule, but it does not explicitly say that performance is used/treated as an index of motivation.
